speakers.name: Deanna Kovar
speakers.title: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag, Sales and Marketing, Regions of the Americas and Australia

exchanges.question: Not an analyst exchange: this numbered block is the scripted management discussion that functions as the prepared remarks. Pooley presents Q3 results, segment results, industry outlook and FY2026 guidance, then asks Seibert, Norwood and Kovar for color on the quarter and tariffs, Construction & Forestry, Small Ag & Turf, Production & Precision Ag by region, model year 2027 early order programs, dealer inventories and precision technology adoption, before Norwood closes.
exchanges.answer: Pooley reported equipment operations operating margin of 14.4%, net sales and revenues up 5% to $12.608 billion, equipment net sales up 6% to $10.999 billion and net income of $1.379 billion or $5.10 per diluted share; FY2026 net income guidance was raised to $4.75 billion-$5 billion, equipment operations cash flow to $5 billion-$5.5 billion and Financial Services net income to $870 million, with PPA sales now down approximately 10% (margin 11%-12%), SAT up approximately 15% (margin raised to 14.5%-15.5%) and C&F up approximately 20% (margin 10.5%-11.5%). Seibert said factories exceeded production expectations, results beat company and consensus expectations, $110 million of incremental IEPA refunds were recognized in Q3 (total $382 million for FY2026, no further refunds assumed) and direct tariff expense is now approximately $1.1 billion for the year excluding refunds after Section 122, 232 and 301 changes; C&F order books are largely full with customer backlogs extending well into FY2027, production modestly below retail, factory-installed SmartGrade adoption up more than 50% year-to-date and job site safety sales up nearly 40%. Norwood said year-to-date performance and a strong fourth quarter order book across all segments allowed narrowed guidance and improved net income and cash flow forecasts, called C&F one of the most significant Leap Ambitions opportunities (including Tenna), and reiterated that 2026 represents the bottom of the ag equipment cycle with a measured, regionally varied recovery. Kovar said PPA demand is softer in South America and Europe but stable at very low levels in North America, order books are effectively full for the year, South America industry was revised to down 15%-20% with modest underproduction of retail there, and the move Agriculture Financing program plus lower rates should help 2027; the model year 2027 sprayer EOP opened mid-May and runs through the end of this month, planters opened at the beginning of June and close at the end of September, the combine program just opened, and collective planter and sprayer orders are up mid-single digits versus the completion of last year's program, with an update next quarter. She added that model-year 2023 and 2024 used high horsepower tractors are down nearly 40% from a year ago and the new-used value spread has largely normalized; See & Spray is on significantly more acres with more than 50% herbicide savings and factory adoption set to nearly double to about 1/3 of North American sprayers on order, more than 40% of North American model year 2027 planters include ExactRate, ExactShot and FurrowVision, Operations Center has more than 520 million engaged acres across nearly 1.2 million connected machines, more than 190 million highly engaged acres (double-digit growth) and more than 450,000 unique active monthly digital users, with AI-enabled capabilities coming soon, and seed, fertilizer and crop protection are roughly 70% of a farmer's operating cost.

exchanges.question: For the 2027 setup, how is Deere thinking about production versus retail by region? And given the early order program is up mid-single digits, what are pricing expectations for 2027 in light of concerns about inflationary farm equipment costs over the past several years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said PPA and C&F are each modestly underproducing retail this year, call it a couple percentage points per segment; shipping plans are set for the full year, changes in South America drive more caution there, and in C&F continued retail growth with an order position four to five months out leads to minor underproduction in 2026. Kovar said EOP pricing was rolled out several months ago and the focus remains on covering inflation with pricing, which has been done across the EOP products and the whole PPA portfolio heading into 2027.

exchanges.question: Is the reduction in expected tariff impact to $1.1 billion, about $100 million below the original estimate, a function of the ag equipment tariff relief in July or of expected refunds? Second, how is the excavator launch trending and when will broader adoption happen?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said the FY2026 direct tariff run rate was previously $1.2 billion and is now $1.1 billion, excluding refunds, driven mainly by Section 232 changes that cut the rate on imported goods from roughly 25% to 15%, notably on imports from Europe; the changes were effective 1st June so only five of 12 months benefit this year, implying a further tailwind in FY2027. Norwood said the first Deere-designed excavator models launched earlier this spring, three models are in the market with very positive customer feedback, shipments are just getting into customers' hands, and additional models in the portfolio will roll out over the next three to four years.

exchanges.question: Did something slip from 4Q into 3Q, and why do inventory-to-sales ratios suggest tractor inventory was built in 3Q ahead of the industry? Is that an offset to demand signals in South America, and what is the cadence exiting the year?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said not to read too much into Q3 changes: shipment plans are largely set for the year with orders on hand, some demand was pulled ahead to manage Q4 risk, and there is nothing concerning on inventory. Kovar said factories are hitting forecasts, sold-ahead positions and retail pace across the Americas are on trend with historical averages, and North America entered the year slowly on tractor shipments (she said 2027) and is making up time while retail pace has not missed. Norwood said PPA and C&F should see Q4 net sales similar to Q3, but Q4 will not have the refund benefit Q3 had and PPA and SAT typically carry a seasonal high of R&D and SA&G in Q4, so margins for those two segments will come in a little.

exchanges.question: How should the mix impact in 2027 be thought about, given higher technology take rates in the early order program and in C&F, versus the 2- to 3-point mix benefit discussed in stronger years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said it is too early to tell: input and commodity volatility, shipment disruptions such as the Black Sea, and recent softness in the E.U. and Brazil need to play out, and construction growth could also affect mix. EOP signals including tech adoption and how the programs wrap up will drive some mix, along with whether the recovery is more than modest and what combines do later this year; he is encouraged by current signals.

exchanges.question: What regional variability in demand did the early order program show, and as it winds down could the current mid-single-digit growth end up in the high single-digit range?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag
exchanges.answer: Kovar said the programs are still open with a couple of weeks left on sprayers and longer on planters; the U.S. is trending slightly better than Canada, which is a very limited part of the planter portfolio. Orders are up mid-single digits and time will tell whether that turns more positive by close. The best signals are technology take rates: See & Spray doubling on factory-installed sprayer orders and 40% of planters taking the most advanced planting technologies.

exchanges.question: What has the cadence of early order program orders looked like since the books opened, and was the mid-single-digit increase driven by recent grain price improvement or technology decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag
exchanges.answer: Kovar said she would not read much into cadence, which has been as expected. Deere made tweaks to the early order program this year to give dealers more choice, orders have come through as expected, technology take rates were a pleasant surprise, and she hopes the mid-single-digit increase extends well into the year.

exchanges.question: Are 8 Series tractor orders tracking the better early order program trend in North America? And in Europe, are crop prices starting to reflect farmer stress from heat and input costs, and would Europe react to a crop price response the way the U.S. does?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said 8R orders are as expected, with orders four to five months out, the model year 2026 shipment schedule basically closed and first-quarter orders now being collected; corn futures at about $5.05 are a good signal for growers. In Brazil Deere takes a three-month order book, has fourth quarter orders on hand, has changed its industry guide, and it is too early to tell on 2027, though the move financing program at single-digit rates could drive momentum. Europe is mixed, with arable farmers more challenged while Small Ag & Turf producers benefit from relatively strong and stable dairy and livestock cash flows; overall order pace is as expected with no step-up in the last one or two days.

exchanges.question: How are the Construction & Forestry order programs shaping up, how much of the strength is dealer rental fleet loading, and what is the outlook for that theme?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said C&F order trends have been very positive with about four to five months of orders on hand, more than the two to three months Deere would typically want, supported by industry and retail growth. Drivers are large infrastructure projects, data center starts, participation in the independent rental channel and the dealer-owned rental fleet opportunity, and the 2026 underproduction gives a little additional opportunity entering 2027.

exchanges.question: With the Section 232 benefit only a half year in 2026 and no further refunds in Q4, is the roughly $800 million net tariff impact this year a headwind, tailwind or neutral going into 2027?
exchanges.answer: Norwood said net tariffs will be a headwind next year: about $1.1 billion of direct tariffs this year less $382 million of refunds gives net exposure of approximately $750-ish million, while the 2027 run rate is expected to be right around $1 billion, so tariff expense steps up next year.

exchanges.question: Why does C&F pricing guidance imply only about 50 basis points of positive price for Q4 versus +8% in Q3? Second, what size does Deere want its dealer rental fleet business to reach and how does it change the economics of the business?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said the C&F price guide started the year at 2.5%, went to 3%, was rounded down to 2.5% and is now back up at the full-year guide; Q3's 8% partly reflected easy comps because Q3 2025 had about 5% negative price from competitive incentives, Q4 orders are on hand with nothing outsized year over year, and pricing including road building is going well. Norwood said 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as a rental and that share keeps growing; dealer-owned fleets have grown with the market and dealers show increased appetite to expand them, a meaningful opportunity that could help boost inventory fill next year, with no target size given.

exchanges.question: On EOP pricing covering inflation, are there merchandising incentives, and does the backlog imply margins up, down or neutral going into next year? Second, what are the implications of the FTC right-to-repair settlement for the aftermarket business and the $2 billion-$3 billion lifecycle parts opportunity over five years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said Deere is taking measured inflationary price in a challenging environment with nothing outsized, committed to covering inflation over time across several pricing points in the year (tractor order book, combine EOP), while the inflationary environment remains dynamic given oil prices and suppliers passing on tariffs; he gave no margin direction. Norwood said Deere has always supported customers' ability to repair their own equipment or use third parties, the agreement formalizes existing tools such as John Deere Operations Center PRO Service (diagnostic tools, digital manuals, self-service software updates or via independent service advisors), and it will support long-term lifecycle solutions aspirations.

exchanges.question: With the European CAP budget policy change set for 2028, could demand be pulled forward into 2027 or delayed until there is certainty, and can Deere give any directional 2027 forecast for Europe?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said it is too early to tell; the order book runs four to five months out and Q1 orders are just starting to be collected. Arable producer sentiment will depend on input costs and commodity prices for next year's crop, dairy and livestock look fairly stable, and it is too early to say whether policy will pull demand forward or delay it.

exchanges.question: How are Brazilian and U.S. farmers positioning on input costs, particularly fertilizer, and how might that affect crop and equipment decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag
exchanges.answer: Kovar said input price uncertainty exists everywhere and fertilizer affects Brazilian and U.S. farmers differently, but markets are reacting and farmers are seeking alternatives in product type, application rates and sourcing. Deere is not seeing a huge reduction in intended application, farmers remain focused on yield, and larger farmers with multiple years of inputs contracted are considering changes; overall farmers remain resilient and nimble.
